The paper under review proposes an "on-the-fly" adaptive framework for speculative decoding, addressing two main components: dynamic window size optimization ($\gamma$) and prompt-feature-based draft model selection. The paper is praised for the novelty of the problem framing (runtime adaptation without heavy training) and the breadth of experimental evaluation across models, hardware, and tasks. However, the review highlights significant technical flaws: a specific accuracy estimator (Eq. 2) is mathematically biased but unanalyzed; the "drop-in" claim is misleading because the draft selection component requires offline calibration on $r$ prompts; and there is a lack of ablation studies isolating the contributions of the two components.
